make slash commands data driven from the widget: today a widget's slash command is derived in `ui/commands.py` (`slash=w.kind`, `takes` when it has a `tool`, `slash_event=("add_widget_ask", w.kind)`), so the name and behaviour are implied, not stated on the widget. idea: put it on the `Widget` class in `ui/widgets.py` (eg its slash name, whether text after it goes to the inline AI, whether it shows in the chat or as a tab). think through the consequences first: `Widget` is about what a value looks like and which tool it wraps, a slash command is about how it is invoked (does that belong on the same class, or does `commands.py` stay the one place for invocation?); the kind doubling as the slash name ties a user-facing word to an internal id (renaming videos -> vods touched both); plain commands (`/help`, `/clear-chat`) have no widget, so there would be two places slash commands come from; and whether "ai widgets" made from a chat query (entry above) should get a slash command the same way

log as close to the source of the request as possible (the http call itself, etc), so a record always has the full details and never depends on the caller remembering to add them. what made me question the current setup: with `@` mentions (branch `exp/at-variables`) the app adds a block to the prompt before it goes to the model, but the debug log's turn record only showed the text i typed, because the "agent" record is written by the caller (`Session.ask`: `log_call("agent", ..., prompt=prompt)`) with whatever it chose to pass; it was patched by adding an `added` field by hand, which is the same weakness again. outside requests don't have this problem: `ds.util.http` / `ds.util.graphql` log at the wrapper, so every record has the request as sent. think through doing the same for AI model requests: one record per model request made at the lowest layer we own (the http client the Gateway provider uses, or a pydantic-ai hook / its instrumentation that Logfire already reads), holding what was really sent (the full messages incl. system instructions, tool definitions, model settings) and what came back, linked to its turn like tool calls are (`tool_call_id`). open questions: size (a long chat's messages on every request: store whole, or cut / diff against the previous request?), secrets, whether the caller-level "agent" record stays as a summary on top, and a rule + test for it like the one that bans direct `httpx2` calls (`.agents/instructions/pkgs.md`, "Each call logs one record")
  - with proper use of loguru's `bind` (and `contextualize`) we should be able to add all the data we want in a maintainable way: the source logs the full request once, and each layer above only binds what it alone knows (session, turn, origin, the mentioned variables, the tool call) so it lands on every record made inside it, instead of each caller hand-building its own record fields. we already do part of this (`logger.contextualize(session=..., origin=...)` in the app, `tool_call_id` in `ds.ai.call_log`, `logger.bind(kind=..., source=..., **fields)` in `ds.util.logging.calls`): work out the one pattern (what is bound where, which names are reserved) and write it down as the rule
